title: Modi Hosts Breakfast for New NDA Allies as Coalition Nears Supermajority
excerpt: Prime Minister Modi welcomed 45 newly elected Rajya Sabha MPs, including rebel Trinamool Congress lawmakers who merged with NCPI, urging them to avoid 'Delhi intrigues' and focus on governance.
body:
• PM Modi hosted 45 new NDA Rajya Sabha MPs for breakfast, including 20 former Trinamool Congress rebels now under the NCPI banner
  • Modi advised MPs to 'avoid the Lutyens web,' learn from senior parliamentarians, and refrain from making inflammatory statements on television
  • The NDA's effective Lok Sabha strength has risen to 318, edging closer to the two-thirds majority needed for constitutional amendments
  • The TMC split — triggered by the party's defeat in the 2026 West Bengal elections — represents the biggest opposition fragmentation in years

Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted a breakfast meeting for 45 newly elected National Democratic Alliance (NDA) Rajya Sabha members, using the gathering to consolidate ties with lawmakers who have dramatically reshaped India's parliamentary arithmetic in recent months.

A New Coalition Takes Shape

The breakfast at the Prime Minister's residence brought together a politically diverse group: BJP's own new Rajya Sabha inductees, former Aam Aadmi Party MPs who crossed over, ex-Uddhav Thackeray faction Shiv Sena lawmakers, and — most significantly — members of the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), a formation built from 20 rebel Trinamool Congress MPs who broke away from Mamata Banerjee's party following its defeat in the 2026 West Bengal assembly elections.

According to ThePrint, NCPI MPs described the meeting as one of "collective identity," with Modi telling the group, "You are all part of the NDA family. No need to worry, I'm with you."

"No one should say anything trashy on TV. Learn from senior MPs, stay clear of Delhi intrigues."

"The group merged with the Tripura-based NCPI to circumvent anti-defection laws, while simultaneously fighting for recognition as the "real" Trinamool Congress in the Supreme Court."

— PM Narendra Modi, as reported by The Times of India

The TMC Split That Changed Everything

The presence of NCPI lawmakers at Modi's breakfast table caps a political upheaval that began on June 2, 2026, when the All India Trinamool Congress fractured after its crushing defeat to the BJP in the West Bengal assembly elections. Mamata Banerjee lost her own Bhabanipur seat to successor Suvendu Adhikari, and the party's organizational collapse followed swiftly.

Within weeks, veteran MP Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar led a group of 20 Lok Sabha MPs — including former cricketer Yusuf Pathan, actress-turned-politician Satabdi Roy, and party heavyweight Sudip Bandyopadhyay — into an alliance with the NDA. The group merged with the Tripura-based NCPI to circumvent anti-defection laws, while simultaneously fighting for recognition as the "real" Trinamool Congress in the Supreme Court.

In the Rajya Sabha, multiple TMC members resigned, including Sukhendu Sekhar Roy and Sushmita Dev. In the West Bengal assembly, 64 of 80 TMC MLAs backed the rival faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee, who was appointed Leader of the Opposition.

NDA Approaches Supermajority

The NCPI's support has boosted the NDA's effective Lok Sabha strength to 318 — within striking distance of the roughly 362 seats needed for a two-thirds majority to pass constitutional amendments. In the Rajya Sabha, the NDA now controls approximately 145 seats in the 244-member house, with the two-thirds mark at 163.

Two major legislative proposals hang in the balance: the Delimitation Bill and the One Nation, One Election framework, both of which require constitutional amendments to proceed.

"We came to know about the progress of the country, about FTAs, farmers. With the data we got, we will be able to make people understand about these issues as well."

— Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, NCPI MP, after attending her first NDA meeting

What It Means for Indian Politics

The TMC split is the most consequential opposition fragmentation since the 2022 Maharashtra political crisis that divided the Shiv Sena. Combined with defections from the Uddhav Thackeray faction — whose MPs also attended Modi's breakfast — the NDA has systematically weakened the INDIA opposition bloc across multiple states.

For the rebel MPs, the calculation is straightforward. As NCPI leader Sudip Bandyopadhyay said after the group's first independent parliamentary meeting, their priority is "the legislative smooth-running of the House and local constituency governance back in West Bengal, rather than escalating local regional disputes to New Delhi."

Whether that pragmatism holds as the NDA pushes for its constitutional ambitions remains the central question of India's current political moment.
nri_angle: The NDA's march toward a supermajority could enable constitutional changes — including delimitation and simultaneous elections — that reshape the democratic framework Indian Americans and NRIs follow closely.
